title: NTT DOCOMO BUSINESS Partners with Classiq to Expand Enterprise Quantum Software Adoption in Japan - Quantum Computing Report
gist: NTT DOCOMO BUSINESS will resell and co-deploy Classiq's hardware-agnostic quantum software platform to Japanese enterprises under an MoU. The deal pairs application-layer software with NTT's 600 km Tokyo-Nagoya-Osaka QKD network to offer an end-to-end quantum-safe-plus-QPU offering.

insights.claim: NTT DOCOMO BUSINESS (formerly NTT Communications) will act as reseller and deployment partner for Classiq's quantum software platform across Japanese manufacturing, finance, logistics and public infrastructure.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Telecom channel partners give quantum software startups enterprise distribution they cannot build alone.
insights.locator: Japanese telecommunications and ICT infrastructure provider

insights.claim: The partners will jointly identify, co-develop and validate industrial gate-based quantum applications with customers.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Early revenue in quantum software is consulting-led use-case discovery.
insights.locator: Under the terms of the agreement

insights.claim: Classiq's platform combines agentic AI interfaces, its Qmod high-level modeling language and an automated synthesis engine that compiles algorithmic intent into circuits optimized for specific hardware.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: AI-assisted, high-level abstraction lowers the expertise barrier for enterprise quantum adoption.
insights.locator: Under the terms of the agreement

insights.claim: Classiq claims hardware-agnostic synthesis lets the same algorithms run on superconducting, neutral-atom, trapped-ion and photonic QPUs without code refactoring.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Hardware-agnostic software layers can capture value regardless of which qubit modality wins.
insights.quote: allowing compiled algorithms to execute across superconducting, neutral-atom, trapped-ion, and photonic QPUs without requiring code refactoring
insights.locator: Under the terms of the agreement

insights.claim: In June 2026 NTT DOCOMO BUSINESS, Toshiba and NEC began building Japan's first wide-area quantum cryptography network, a 600 km QKD and secret-sharing network spanning Tokyo, Nagoya and Osaka under MIC and NICT.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: National QKD infrastructure build-out is a tangible spending line for Japanese telecom/equipment vendors.

insights.claim: NTT's quantum strategy is motivated by mitigating Harvest Now, Decrypt Later risks and supporting post-quantum cryptography validation.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: HNDL fear is driving security spend before quantum computers can break encryption.

insights.claim: By combining its QKD backbone and Quantum Secure Cloud with Classiq's synthesis engine, NTT DOCOMO BUSINESS pitches an end-to-end stack from quantum-safe security to QPU application development.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Telcos are positioning as integrators of the full quantum value chain in Japan.
insights.locator: By pairing this wide-area QKD backbone
